findings.text: a local variable merely named like a guarded symbol counts as a declaration, so a module that never held the grammar reddens the uniqueness guard. Concrete input: a new module imas_ambix/agent/label_surface.py containing only `def split_labels(text):` / `    _SAMPLE_RE = text.split(',')` / `    _bare_metric_name = str` / `    return _SAMPLE_RE, _bare_metric_name(text)`. Against a scratch copy of the reviewed package this fails 2 of the 6 guard tests on an all_debug allocation -- test_exposition_grammar_has_one_owner naming 'imas_ambix/agent/label_surface.py' as an extra definer of _SAMPLE_RE, and test_no_retired_reader_symbol_survives on _bare_metric_name -- measured 2 failed, 4 passed in 8.80s (scratch/logs/fp-local-name.log). The scan's carve-out for reuse covers imports only (tests/test_agent_bench_shared_reader.py:171 says so); on the assignment side a name reuse reads as a second owner, and the retired-symbol test at tests/test_agent_bench_shared_reader.py:135, whose docstring says the privates are 'gone, not shadowed', fires on a module that never contained the retired helper. Reproduced by probe too (logs/shape-probe.log, case local-var-named-like and local-retired-name).

three behaviours the repair states are unasserted; each mutation leaves the suite green (6 passed, on an all_debug allocation). (1) the guarded set itself: narrowing `for symbol in ("_SAMPLE_RE", "_LABEL_RE", "parse_metrics"):` at :122 to the first two symbols leaves 6 passed (scratch/logs/mut-m7-guarded-set-narrowed.log), so the claim that all six symbols are covered is held by nothing and a future edit that drops a symbol narrows the guard silently. (2) the parse-error claim: the comment at :111-113 states that a parse error is a real defect rather than a file to step over; wrapping `tree = ast.parse(...)` at :114 in `except SyntaxError: continue` (the mutation the comment forbids) leaves 6 passed (scratch/logs/mut-m6-parse-error-swallowed.log). (3) the tuple/list branch of _target_names at :64-68 is dead weight: deleting it leaves 6 passed (scratch/logs/mut-m4-no-tuple-unpacking.log); no fixture uses a tuple or list target.

limit of the widened signature, recorded rather than repaired: the node forms _declares visits are def/async def/class/Assign/AnnAssign/NamedExpr, so a binding by augmented assignment, by `except Exception as parse_metrics`, by a for or with target, by a parameter name, or by a `globals()["parse_metrics"] = ...` subscript is not a declaration and a rival spelled that way is invisible (probes: logs/shape-probe.log, logs/shape-probe3.log). The three shapes the brief names are all caught. The import-as-alias form is deliberately not a declaration.

the landing comment and the evidence record's Gates paragraph both state 'both runs on an all_debug allocation', while the node's own manifest discloses a third run of the same three-file suite on the login node (after-suite.log, 70.11s, not offered as the gate, and the manifest says so). The sentence is true of the two offered runs; read alone it says no login-node run happened, which is not the case. The manifest is the honest half of this pair.
